_comment: Illustrative posts used by `npm run scan:sample` so the dashboard renders end-to-end WITHOUT live API credentials. These are NOT real posts — every item carries isSample:true and links to the profile, not a specific status. The `comment` field is a curated learn-wise example; in live mode comments are written by Claude (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or the template fallback.

@karpathy.text: The best way to understand something deeply is to build it from scratch once, even badly. Abstractions are great for shipping, terrible for learning.
@karpathy.comment: The "build it from scratch once, even badly" rule keeps proving itself for me — I only really understood tokenization after writing a clumsy one by hand. Good reminder that abstractions ship code but rarely teach it. 🧠

@garrytan.text: Conviction is easy on a good week. The founders who make it are the ones whose belief survives contact with a bad one.
@garrytan.comment: The split between conviction on a good week vs. a bad one is the part I'm keeping. It reframes resilience as something you pre-decide rather than something you have to summon in the moment.

y-combinator-community.text: Office hours reminder: talk to your users every week, not every quarter. Treat user research as a habit, not a milestone.
y-combinator-community.comment: Treating user research as a weekly habit instead of a quarterly milestone is a small reframe that compounds — going to block a recurring slot for it this week. 🙏

y-combinator.text: Default alive or default dead? It's a question you answer with a spreadsheet and your real burn — not a vibe. Know your number.
y-combinator.comment: The nudge to answer "default alive or dead" with the actual burn spreadsheet, not a gut feeling, landed for me. Turning a vague worry into a number you can act on is the useful move.
